synthesis.evidence_balance: mixed — a near-floor multiple against rising EBITDA, strong ROIC and accelerating CV, offset by flat revenue, declining new business and a walked-back growth target.

bull_points.claim: The de-rate is an optical multiple collapse against RISING fundamentals: TEV/LTM EBITDA sits at 9.4x, its own 5-year ~5th percentile (range 7.5–37.8x, median 23.0x), yet LTM EBITDA RISES to $1,421M from $1,311M a year prior — the multiple fell while absolute EBITDA grew, the overshoot-vs-terminal question the human must weigh.

historical_forecast_error.usage_note: EBIT- or EBITDA-level shock today: error_per_forecast_revenue × today's revenue consensus. Exact identity: error_per_forecast_revenue = ratio_error + (actual ÷ actual revenue) × (actual revenue ÷ forecast revenue − 1).

R1 pairs that median with the median multiple from the same history, so an R1 value answers what the business is worth if it is still what it was. If the gap is STRUCTURAL — a changed mix or model — that history understates it; if it is a cyclical PEAK, reverting is right. On FY2025 the two sources differ by 2.4 points (GAAP 15.8% vs CIQ 18.1%): GAAP carries charges CIQ's EBIT excludes, and R1's median sits on the GAAP side, so part of this gap may be basis, not business.
